"""Lab 02 - build small circuits with X, H and measure, run them, read the counts.

Run:  python gates_lab.py
"""
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler   # Qiskit's reference sampler; Aer's SamplerV2 is an equivalent


def build_circuits():
    """Return {name: circuit}. Every circuit ends with measure_all() -> register 'meas'."""
    circuits = {}

    qc = QuantumCircuit(1)          # qubits start in |0>
    qc.measure_all()
    circuits["nothing"] = qc        # always '0'

    qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
    qc.x(0)                         # X = NOT: |0> -> |1>
    qc.measure_all()
    circuits["x"] = qc              # always '1'

    qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
    qc.h(0)                         # superposition: H gives amplitudes (0.7071, 0.7071)
    qc.measure_all()                # Born rule: P = |amplitude|^2 -> 50% '0', 50% '1'
    circuits["h"] = qc

    qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
    qc.h(0)
    qc.h(0)                         # interference: H twice undoes itself -> always '0'
    qc.measure_all()
    circuits["h_h"] = qc

    qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
    qc.x(0)                         # flip qubit 0 only
    qc.measure_all()
    circuits["x_on_q0_of_2"] = qc   # bit order: prints '01', qubit 0 is the RIGHTMOST bit

    return circuits


def run_all(shots=1000, seed=7):
    """Run every circuit on the local reference sampler; return {name: counts}."""
    circuits = build_circuits()
    names = list(circuits)
    sampler = StatevectorSampler(seed=seed)   # fixed seed -> same counts every run
    result = sampler.run([circuits[n] for n in names], shots=shots).result()
    return {name: result[i].data.meas.get_counts() for i, name in enumerate(names)}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(build_circuits()["h"].draw())   # text drawing of the H circuit
    for name, counts in run_all().items():
        print(f"{name:14s} {dict(sorted(counts.items()))}")

code:
"""Lab 03 - shots, counts and probability: why results vary and how a seed makes them repeatable.

Run:  python shots_lab.py
"""
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler   # Qiskit's reference sampler; Aer's SamplerV2 is an equivalent


def coin_circuit():
    """One qubit in equal superposition: ideal P('0') = P('1') = 0.5."""
    qc = QuantumCircuit(1)
    qc.h(0)
    qc.measure_all()
    return qc


def sample(shots, seed=None):
    """Run `shots` repetitions. seed=None -> new random stream each call."""
    sampler = StatevectorSampler(seed=seed)    # seed: replays the same random draws; does not make them more accurate
    result = sampler.run([coin_circuit()], shots=shots).result()   # shot noise: each shot is one random draw
    counts = result[0].data.meas.get_counts()
    return {"0": counts.get("0", 0), "1": counts.get("1", 0)}


def text_histogram(counts, width=40):
    """Tiny terminal histogram: one '#' per (total/width) shots."""
    total = sum(counts.values())
    return "\n".join(f"{k} | {'#' * round(width * v / total):<{width}} {v}" for k, v in sorted(counts.items()))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for shots in (10, 100, 1000, 10000):
        c = sample(shots, seed=42)
        # estimate = count / shots; its standard error shrinks like 1/sqrt(shots)
        print(f"shots={shots:<6d} counts={c}  estimated P('1')={c['1'] / shots:.3f}")
    print("\nunseeded, run 1:", sample(100))     # these two usually differ
    print("unseeded, run 2:", sample(100))
    print("seeded 2024, run 1:", sample(100, seed=2024))  # these two are identical
    print("seeded 2024, run 2:", sample(100, seed=2024))
    print("\n" + text_histogram(sample(1000, seed=42)))

equivalents: Same idea in Cirq: `cirq.Simulator(seed=42).run(circuit, repetitions=1000)` then `result.histogram(key='m')`.
Qiskit Aer (Apache-2.0, 'reduced maintenance mode'): `qiskit_aer.primitives.SamplerV2(seed=7)` takes the same PUBs; use it for noise models or speed.
Plain numpy: `np.random.default_rng(seed).binomial(shots, p)` (see crosscheck_numpy.py).

Microsoft QDK / Q# (MIT): same operations written in Q#, run locally from Python via the `qdk` package.
inRealSystems: Qiskit StatevectorSampler(seed=...) (used here) and Aer SamplerV2(seed=...) take shots and seeds; Cirq uses repetitions with cirq.Simulator(seed=...); PennyLane sets qp.set_shots (shots=None gives exact statistics); CI suites, including this repo's, compare with tolerances (5 sigma).
useWhen: Seed for unit tests, demos, docs output and bug reproduction; leave unseeded when estimating real variability or benchmarking, and never expect a seed to match across frameworks.
simulatorVsReal: Runs on Qiskit's reference StatevectorSampler (qiskit 2.6.1), an ideal (noise-free) local simulator. Real hardware adds noise, so outcomes that are impossible here (e.g. '01' for a Bell pair) appear with small counts. Hardware results also drift between runs; a seed only fixes simulator sampling.

title: Entanglement with a Bell pair
description: Build H + CNOT, run it, and check that only '00' and '11' appear.

code:
"""Lab 05 - portable circuits: export to OpenQASM 3 (and 2), re-import, compare.

Run:  python qasm_lab.py
Needs: qiskit, qiskit-qasm3-import (qasm3.loads depends on it).
"""
from pathlib import Path

from qiskit import QuantumCircuit, qasm2, qasm3
from qiskit.primitives import StatevectorSampler   # Qiskit's reference sampler; Aer's SamplerV2 is an equivalent
from qiskit.quantum_info import Operator


def bell_circuit(measure=True):
    qc = QuantumCircuit(2)
    qc.h(0)
    qc.cx(0, 1)
    if measure:
        qc.measure_all()
    return qc


def roundtrip_qasm3(qc):
    text = qasm3.dumps(qc)          # portability: QuantumCircuit -> neutral OpenQASM 3 text
    return text, qasm3.loads(text)  # round-trip: text -> new QuantumCircuit


def roundtrip_qasm2(qc):
    text = qasm2.dumps(qc)          # older, simpler format; still widely accepted
    return text, qasm2.loads(text)


def same_unitary(a, b):
    """True if two measurement-free circuits do the same thing (up to global phase)."""
    return Operator(a).equiv(Operator(b))   # unitary equivalence: compare behaviour, not text


def counts(qc, shots=1000, seed=7):
    result = StatevectorSampler(seed=seed).run([qc], shots=shots).result()
    register = qc.cregs[0].name                  # 'meas' from measure_all(); read it, don't assume
    return getattr(result[0].data, register).get_counts()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    text3, back3 = roundtrip_qasm3(bell_circuit())
    print(text3)
    out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "bell.qasm"   # the neutral artifact you can share
    out.write_text(text3, encoding="utf-8")
    text2, _ = roundtrip_qasm2(bell_circuit())
    print(text2)
    _, gates_only = roundtrip_qasm3(bell_circuit(measure=False))
    print("qasm3 round-trip same unitary:", same_unitary(bell_circuit(False), gates_only))
    print("qasm2 round-trip same unitary:", same_unitary(bell_circuit(False), roundtrip_qasm2(bell_circuit(False))[1]))
    print("original counts:  ", counts(bell_circuit()))
    print("re-imported counts:", counts(back3))   # same seed -> expected identical

conceptSummary: Qiskit and Cirq share gates and physics but differ in conventions: Qiskit bitstrings are little-endian, Cirq histograms big-endian, and each has its own RNG. Normalise bit order and compare distributions, using an asymmetric probe to catch ordering bugs.
